samples.summary: No test that a batch which genuinely writes DROPS redo — the negative half of the `priorRedo` restore is uncovered
samples.evidence: The delta moves redo-clearing out of `snapshot()`/`batch()` and into `willWrite()`, and `batch()`'s finally block restores `this.redoStack = priorRedo` only when `wroteNothing` (memory.ts:287-300). Every new/existing redo test covers the restore side: 'a batch that writes nothing leaves redo history intact' (line 382), 'a self-reverting batch leaves redo history intact' (line 402), 'snapshot() then a batch that writes nothing leaves redo intact' (line 440), and 'a write after an adopted empty batch still drops redo' (line 459 — the write is OUTSIDE the batch). I grepped every `canRedo` assertion in packages/docs/test (results: memory.test.ts lines 170,175,181,186,190,392,396,408,416,449,454,468,474) and none is of the shape `undo(); batch(() => { realWrite() }); expect(canRedo()).toBe(false)`. If the `wroteNothing` guard on the restore were ever wrong (e.g. restore made unconditional), the suite would stay green while a redo after a real batched edit reapplies a stale branch state over the document — silent data loss for the user.

samples.summary: `willWrite()` added to ~26 mutators but redo-clearing is only exercised through insertText/deleteText/insertBlock
samples.evidence: The diff inserts `this.willWrite()` into setDocument, replaceDocument, updateBlock, insertBlock(After/sAfter), deleteBlock(ByIndex), setPageSetup, setDocStyles, updateStyleDefinition, resetStyle, resetAllStyles, setHeader, setFooter, all six table ops, insertText, deleteText, applyStyle, splitBlock, mergeBlock, setBlockType, applyBlockStyle, applyCellStyle, applyCellSpan, insertImageInline. The only tests that observe redo clearing are line 164 ('should clear redo stack on new snapshot', via insertBlock) and line 459 (via insertText). Nothing pins the invariant 'every mutator invalidates redo', so a mutator added later (or one that loses the call in a refactor) would let a redo entry survive a write and, on Cmd+Y, replace the document with a state that branch no longer leads to. A single table-driven test over the mutator list would close it.

samples.summary: Existing test 'should clear redo stack on new snapshot' no longer tests what its name claims after this delta
samples.evidence: `snapshot()` no longer clears redo (the `this.redoStack = []` line was removed from it in this diff, memory.ts:214-220). The test at line 164 does `store.snapshot(); store.insertBlock(...)` and then asserts `canRedo() === false`, so it now passes purely because of `insertBlock`'s new `willWrite()`; it would pass identically if `snapshot()` did or did not clear redo. It is stale coverage advertising a contract this delta deliberately reversed — the new test at line 440 asserts the opposite. Rename/retarget it so the suite does not document a rule the code no longer follows.

samples.summary: The documented 'called before the mutation so a throwing method leaves no redo entry' rule has no test, and the mutators are inconsistent about it
samples.evidence: memory.ts:205-208 states willWrite runs before the mutation specifically so a method that throws part-way leaves no applicable redo entry. No test exercises that: the throwing-mutator tests (memory.test.ts:571 insertText on a missing block, :589 applyStyle, :745 mergeBlock across regions, :76 deleteBlockByIndex out of bounds) all assert only that a throw happens, never the redo stack afterwards. The behaviour is also not uniform — `deleteBlockByIndex` (line 106) and `mergeBlock` (line 383) validate before calling willWrite (redo survives), while `insertText`/`applyStyle` clear redo then throw — and nothing records which is intended.

samples.summary: 'a batch that writes nothing keeps the checkpoint it adopted' asserts only stack depth, not that the adopted checkpoint holds the right state
samples.evidence: The test snapshots, runs `batch(() => {})`, asserts canUndo true, undoes, asserts canUndo false. Since nothing was ever written, the document reads 'Hello' before and after the undo, so the test cannot distinguish a correct adopted checkpoint from a garbage one — it only counts entries. The companion test at line 421 does check content, so the gap is contained; adding a document assertion after the `undo()` here would make it self-sufficient.

samples.summary: The cross-store parity claim this delta is built on ('YorkieDocStore keeps redo across snapshot() + empty batch') is asserted only in comments, never tested
samples.evidence: memory.ts:192-208 and the new tests at memory.test.ts:440 justify the redo-semantics change entirely by what `YorkieDocStore` does. In the Yorkie suite, `canRedo` appears only at lines 324, 337, 344-354, and the batch section's closest test is 'an empty batch pushes no undo unit' (line 875) which checks `getUndoStackForTest().length` only. verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: redo-clearing now lives in willWrite() (memory.ts:210-212, called from every mutator, e.g. 305/350/362) and batch() restores priorRedo only under the wroteNothing guard (memory.ts:265, 287-300). Tests cover only the restore half — empty batch (memory.test.ts:382-400), self-reverting batch (402-419), snapshot()+empty batch (440-457) — and the drop half only for writes OUTSIDE a batch (164-176; and 459-475 where the insertText at 472 is after the batch closes at 471). I enumerated every canRedo assertion and every .redo() call in every test file repo-wide: none performs undo(); batch(() => realWrite()); then asserts canRedo()===false or that redo() is a no-op on a MemDocStore. Editor-level redo tests (pending-style-editor.test.ts:208-224, caret-line-affinity.test.ts:255-274, copy-integrity.test.ts:1103-1118, text-box-editor.test.ts:351-359) all have no store write between undo and redo, so they cannot catch it; frontend docs redo tests exercise YorkieDocStore and the slides canRedo tests exercise MemSlidesStore. Making the restore unconditional would leave the suite green while redo after any real batched edit (the path every editor op takes via withUndoUnit -> batch) reapplies a stale branch state over the document — silent data-affecting corruption, hence blocking under the test-adequacy rubric.
